audit_2026_10_31: FRESH AUDIT PASSED (first-hand, 2026-10-31) — the expansion order's next county after the WAVE1 five completed 2026-10-29 and the same night's Georgia candidates (Fulton/Atlanta no record-level feed; DeKalb issued population collapsed; Forsyth IssueDate unpopulated; Columbus GA dead since 2021; Johns Creek dead since 2019), Michigan candidates (Grand Rapids Socrata decommissioned; Detroit BSEED building layer issuance cliff June 2026 + trades layer irreconcilable group-by populations and non-permit case records; Ann Arbor/Lansing/Kalamazoo/Flint no usable feed), and Durham NC (internal ArcGIS Online view, not a public source) all failed pre-build verification. (1) Source: City of Pittsburgh PLI Permits on the Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center (CKAN), package pli-permits, one datastore-active CSV resource (f4d1177a-f597-4c32-8cbf-7885f56253f6) — the catalog's own documented query route, the same adapter family as San Antonio. 66,559 rows all-time; the resource's last_modified stamp is 2026-10-31T03:20:18Z (the city's ETL reloads it on a daily cadence). (2) SNAPSHOT INCIDENT, measured and resolved: the datastore SQL API first served this audit a stale snapshot of the register (the pre-Accela taxonomy — BUILDING/HVAC/OCCUPANCY families, 8,109 window rows) consistently for roughly 25 minutes, then flipped to the current table (Accela-era families and ids: BDA/EP/MP...). Every figure in this registry comes from the CURRENT table, verified three independent ways after the flip: the pipeline's own pre-pull count and full pull, a field-level DB cross-check against fresh source queries (window total, September 2026, type and prefix distributions, monthly series — all exact), and two further stability recount passes (total 66,559 / window 9,758 each time). The nightly refresh's gate 4 (count-match plus baseline) guards every future pull; a flap back would surface as drift and mass record replacement. (3) VOLUME STABILITY by issue_date year (current table): 8,804 (2022) / 9,300 / 9,124 / 9,159 (2025) / 8,262 (2026 YTD through Oct 29) — steady, no collapse. Trailing-12-month window (issue_date >= 2025-10-31): 9,758 rows; September 2026: 881; October 2026 to date: 867; newest issue_date 2026-10-29. (4) Identity measured on the full window: 9,758 rows = 9,758 distinct permit_id, 0 duplicates, 0 nulls. (5) Population: the pull excludes the register's Plan Review Meeting family (9 window rows) — pre-application meeting records, not issued permits (the San Antonio pull-time family exclusion); the published window is 9,749 permits. Every published row carries an issue date; window statuses are post-issuance or amendment-workflow states (Issued 5,403 / Completed 4,230 / Revoked 51 / amendment and finalization states 74 — across the full 9,758-row window). (6) Coverage is City-of-Pittsburgh-issued permits only: Pittsburgh's Department of Permits, Licenses & Inspections (PLI) issues for the city; Allegheny County's other municipalities issue their own permits and are not in this feed — labeled as such on the hub (the Chicago/Cook treatment). (7) Terms: the package license is CC BY 4.0; publisher City of Pittsburgh via the Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center.
coverage_note: Permits issued by the City of Pittsburgh only. Allegheny County's other municipalities issue their own permits through their own systems and they are not in this feed; totals here are City of Pittsburgh totals, labeled as such.

dedupe_rule.definition: One published permit = one permit_id in the City of Pittsburgh PLI register. The register's grain is one row per permit (no component fan-out, no merged second record kind), and the pull window is issue_date, which only issued permits carry, so applications that were never issued never enter the pull and no collapsing applies or is needed. One family is excluded at pull time (registry pull_where_extra, the San Antonio treatment): Plan Review Meeting records (PLI-MTG ids) are pre-application meetings, not permits — they carry no permit character (one window record's address is literally 'No primary address specified') and they restate the underlying project's declared value, so they are not permits in this report.
dedupe_rule.measurement: Trailing-12-month window (issue_date >= 2025-10-31), measured 2026-10-31 through the CKAN datastore SQL API on the current table (see audit snapshot note): 9,758 rows = 9,758 distinct permit_id, 0 duplicates, 0 nulls; minus the 9 Plan Review Meeting records = 9,749 published permits. The pipeline's in-batch duplicate gate and the (county_id, source_record_id) upsert key guard every future pull.

field_map.address: address, as published ('5112 CHAPLAIN Way, Pittsburgh, PA 15207-'): the street portion before the first comma is carried as the address (whitespace collapsed; all-caps values title-cased) — present on all 9,749 published window permits. City is Pittsburgh (the issuing jurisdiction) on every record; ZIP comes from the register's own zip_code field (present on 9,748 of 9,749).
field_map.application_date: The register publishes no application-date field, so application_date stays NULL by construction (the Philadelphia treatment).
field_map.category: commercial_or_residential, the city's own class for each permit: Residential 6,162 / Commercial 3,586 / unstated 10 across the full window — carried on 99.9% of published permits.
field_map.contractor_rule: contractor_name is carried exactly as PLI publishes it — the permit's contractor of record (businesses and licensed sole proprietors as the register names them; present on 4,945 of 9,749 published window permits, the empty string carries as NULL). The register's owner_name field is a property-owner person-name field: it is excluded from pull_select and never requested from the API at all.
field_map.issue_date: issue_date (an ISO date string in the datastore). The window is defined on it: a record enters this report when PLI records an issue date.
field_map.permit_number: permit_id (unique in the window, see dedupe_rule).
field_map.permit_type: permit_type, the city's own permit family (Building & Development Application / ELECTRICAL / MECHANICAL / Suppression System Permit / Fire Alarm Permit / Demolition Permit / Sign Permit / Floodplain Permit / Storm Water Permit / Land Operations Permit / the occupancy families / the legacy BUILDING family), read together with work_type for the trade classification — see trades.classify_pittsburgh_trade: PLI names the licensed trades itself, so classification starts from the family; only inside the two building families does a New Construction work type split out new construction.
field_map.status: status, the permit's current status, mapped through status_map; the verbatim source value is kept in status_source. Window statuses (full 9,758-row window): Issued 5,403 / Completed 4,230 / Revoked 51, plus amendment-workflow states on already-issued permits (Application Finalization 31, Amendment Applicant Revisions 15, Amendment Review 9, Ready For Issue 7, Amendment Application Incomplete 6, Amendment Requested 4, Applicant Revisions 2) — every published record carries an issue date, so post-issuance and amendment states stay in the population (the Raleigh treatment).
field_map.valuation: total_project_value FAILED validation on the full window (measured 2026-10-31 on the current table) and is NOT carried: valuation stays NULL and Pittsburgh publishes counts only. Evidence: the field is the PROJECT's declared value restated across the project's records, the Miami-Dade disease — the same address states the same value of $100,000 or more on two permits at 10 or more window addresses (946 Saw Mill Run Blvd $8,000,000 twice; 1233 Mifflin Rd $7,600,000 twice; 900 Art Rooney Ave $4,400,000 twice; two casino addresses twice each), and the register's largest stated figures sit on records that are not construction permits at all: a $71,989,164 occupant-load placard (3701 5th Ave) and a $42,000,000 plan-review meeting record for a project whose building permit states $48,925,219. No trustworthy aggregate exists, so per the Austin/Miami-Dade precedent the pages ship without any dollar figure and the reason is stated on the Data Sources page. The raw field stays out of the pull entirely (it is not in pull_select), and is re-validated only if the source's field changes character.

history_range: issue_date 1993 onward in the source (66,559 rows); we backfill the trailing 12 months only (site rule).

terms_status: verified-open-2026-10-31: the WPRDC catalog record for 'PLI Permits' (package pli-permits; organization: City of Pittsburgh; access public) carries the CC BY 4.0 license; figures are published 'as reported by the City of Pittsburgh' with attribution; no endorsement is implied.
update_cadence: Daily (city ETL reloads the datastore resource; MEASURED 2026-10-31: resource last_modified 2026-10-31T03:20:18Z and newest issue_date 2026-10-29 — a two-day issuance lag at audit time). Freshness (gate 5) is measured as the datastore resource's last_modified stamp from package_show under a 96h threshold (the San Antonio treatment). The max issue date is re-verified at every refresh.
watermark_field: issue_date + permit_id — refresh re-pulls by the issue_date watermark and upserts.
